conceptBreakdown.heading: 4.1 de Broglie Matter-Wave Duality (1924)
conceptBreakdown.title: 4.1 de Broglie Matter-Wave Duality (1924)

summaryBox.title: Matter Wave Duality
summaryBox.takeaway: All moving matter has wave character: λ = h/p = h/(mv). For accelerated electrons: λ_e = 12.27 / √V Å.

conceptBreakdown.content:
Louis de Broglie proposed that moving material particles exhibit wave-particle duality:

$$\mathbf{\lambda = \frac{h}{p} = \frac{h}{m v} = \frac{h}{\sqrt{2 m E_k}} = \frac{h}{\sqrt{2 m q V}}}$$

• **Accelerated Electron Formula**: For an electron accelerated from rest across potential difference $V$ Volts:

$$\mathbf{\lambda_e = \frac{12.27}{\sqrt{V}} \text{ \AA} = \sqrt{\frac{150}{V}} \text{ \AA} = \frac{1.227}{\sqrt{V}} \text{ nm}}$$

• **Bohr-de Broglie Connection**: Standing wave condition requires constructive interference along the circular orbit:

$$2\pi r = n \lambda \implies 2\pi r = n \left( \frac{h}{m_e v} \right) \implies \mathbf{m_e v r = \frac{n h}{2\pi}}$$

Thus, Bohr's empirical angular momentum quantization is naturally explained as a standing matter wave condition with $n$ full wavelengths.

conceptBreakdown.heading: 4.2 Heisenberg Uncertainty Principle (1927)
conceptBreakdown.title: 4.2 Heisenberg Uncertainty Principle (1927)
conceptBreakdown.codeSnippet:
HEISENBERG UNCERTAINTY EQUATIONS

   Position-Momentum: Δx · Δp_x ≥ h / 4π = ℏ / 2
   Position-Velocity: Δx · (m Δv_x) ≥ h / 4π
   Energy-Time:       ΔE · Δt ≥ h / 4π = ℏ / 2
conceptBreakdown.content:
It is physically impossible to measure simultaneously both the exact position and exact momentum (or velocity) of a subatomic particle:

$$\mathbf{\Delta x \cdot \Delta p_x \ge \frac{h}{4\pi} = \frac{\hbar}{2}}$$
$$\mathbf{\Delta x \cdot (m \Delta v_x) \ge \frac{h}{4\pi}}$$
$$\mathbf{\Delta E \cdot \Delta t \ge \frac{h}{4\pi}}$$

• **Proof of Non-existence of Free Electrons in the Nucleus**:
Nuclear diameter is $\Delta x \approx 10^{-14}\text{ m}$. For an electron ($m_e = 9.1 \times 10^{-31}\text{ kg}$):

$$\Delta v \ge \frac{h}{4\pi m_e \Delta x} = \frac{6.626 \times 10^{-34}}{4\pi \times (9.1 \times 10^{-31}) \times 10^{-14}} \approx 5.7 \times 10^{10}\text{ m/s}$$

Since $\Delta v > 3 \times 10^8\text{ m/s}$ ($c$, speed of light), which violates special relativity, free electrons cannot reside inside the nucleus.
